messages:
Alex P.: Proposal: build a routecard materialized table (routecard_v1) to replace the three-way join query the console uses. Goal = cut console p99 by 40% for list pages. Plan = seed bulk import + streaming delta + staged read-probe canary.
Maya R.: Nice. What fields go in routecard_v1? We need to ensure it covers the small set the UI needs (title, quota_score, last_active, tags, health_state).
Alex P.: Exactly. Minimal denorm: route_id, tenant_id, title, quota_score, last_seen_at, is_restricted, tags_json, health_state, updated_at. No giant blobs.
Sam K.: How will we keep it up-to-date? I prefer a streaming bridge (kafka -> consumer -> write) rather than touching the canonical writer. Shadow-write from writer for parity during rollout.
Irene L.: Streaming bridge + idempotent writer works. For seed: export route_profiles snapshot to S3 and run parallel importer. Then stream deltas to sync.
Jordan S.: Read adapter semantics: prefer routecard_v1 when row exists and updated_at within staleness window (default 5m). If missing or stale, fall back to join path. This avoids weird UI flicker.
Maya R.: Staleness windows: 5m for live UI, 1h for exports. We should make it configurable per route and per page type.
Alex P.: Canary steps: 1) seed import 2) enable shadow-write for 48h 3) enable read-probe for 1% of tenant requests (compare results) 4) if mismatch <0.05% and p99 improves, widen to 20% then 100%. Rollback by disabling read adapter.
Sam K.: Important metrics: mismatch rate, hydrate lag, stream consumer lag, routecard write error rate, console p99, console 5xx. Also watch DB IOPS and write stalls.
Irene L.: Add automated gate: if mismatch_rate > 0.1% OR console p99 increases >15% sustained 5m OR stream lag > 30s, auto-disable read-probe and page #incidents.
Jordan S.: SQL check to compare ordering (sample tenant):
```sql
-- compare top-100 ordering between v1 and join
WITH v AS (
  SELECT route_id, quota_score FROM routecard_v1 WHERE tenant_id = 'T123' ORDER BY quota_score DESC LIMIT 100
), j AS (
  SELECT rp.route_id, compute_quota(rp.*) AS quota_score FROM route_profiles rp WHERE tenant_id = 'T123' ORDER BY quota_score DESC LIMIT 100
)
SELECT count(1) FROM v JOIN j USING (route_id) WHERE v.quota_score != j.quota_score;
```
Maya R.: Population size? We have ~90M routes across tenants. Hydrate time at 100k/s ~900s (~15m) not counting backoff. We'll do parallel workers across shards.
Sam K.: Consider backpressure: importer should respect DB RPS and avoid hot partitions. Add jitter and pace per shard.
Alex P.: Retention: routecard_v1 TTL 90 days, compaction weekly. Archive to glacier-equivalent and keep lineage keys for rebuild.
Irene L.: Tests: property-based tests for idempotency, consumer replay handling, and a lifting test where we simulate 5% mismatches and ensure auto-gate triggers.
Jordan S.: Runbook snippets for rollback:
```
-- disable read adapter
UPDATE flags SET value = 'false' WHERE name = 'routecard_read_adapter_enabled';
-- stop shadow-write consumer
kubectl scale deployment/routecard-writer --replicas=0 -n prod
```
Sam K.: Who's oncall for first 24h of canary? Maya volunteered?
Maya R.: I'll take first 12h, Alex takes the next 12h.
